verses.text: Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bikri, from the tribe of Benjamin, happened to be there. He blew a trumpet and shouted, "We have no share in David! We have no part in Jesse's son! Everyone go home, Israel!"
So all the men of Israel left David and followed Sheba son of Bikri. But the men of Judah stayed with their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

When David came back to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten slave wives he had left to take care of the palace and put them in a house under guard. He gave them food, but he did not sleep with them again. They were kept shut away until the day they died, living like widows.
Then the king said to Amasa, "Call the men of Judah together within three days, and be here yourself."
So Amasa went to call the men of Judah together, but he took longer than the time the king had given him.
David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bikri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take my men and go after him, before he gets into strong walled cities and escapes from us."
So Joab's men, the Kerethites, the Pelethites, and all the strongest fighters, left Jerusalem with Abishai to chase Sheba son of Bikri.

When they reached the large rock at Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his soldier's uniform, with a belt around his waist and a sword in its sheath. As he stepped forward, the sword fell out.
Joab said to Amasa, "How are you, my brother?" Then Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him.

Amasa did not notice the sword in Joab's other hand. Joab stabbed him in the stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab did not need to strike him again, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai went on chasing Sheba son of Bikri.
One of Joab's young men stood beside Amasa's body and shouted, "Whoever supports Joab and whoever is for David, follow Joab!"

Amasa lay in the middle of the road, rolling in his own blood. The man saw that all the soldiers were stopping to look. So he dragged Amasa's body off the road into a field and threw a cloth over it, because everyone who came by was stopping.
Once the body was moved off the road, all the men went on with Joab to chase Sheba son of Bikri.
Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth Maacah, and through the whole area of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.
Joab's men came and surrounded Sheba in Abel of Beth Maacah. They built a ramp of earth up against the city wall, and all the soldiers with Joab began battering the wall to knock it down.
Then a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him."
Joab came near, and the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" He answered, "I am." She said to him, "Listen to what your servant has to say." He answered, "I am listening."
She said, "In the old days people used to say, 'Go and get advice from Abel,' and that is how they settled their problems.
We are peaceful and faithful people in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is like a mother in Israel. Why do you want to swallow up what belongs to the LORD?"
Joab answered, "Never! I would never swallow up or destroy anything!

That is not what this is about. A man named Sheba son of Bikri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has rebelled against King David. Just hand him over, and I will leave the city." The woman said to Joab, "His head will be thrown to you over the wall."

Then the woman went to all the people with her wise advice. They cut off the head of Sheba son of Bikri and threw it out to Joab. So Joab blew the trumpet, and his men left the city and went home. And Joab went back to the king in Jerusalem.
Joab was in charge of the whole army of Israel. Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Kerethites and Pelethites.
Adoniram was in charge of the forced labour. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.
Sheva was the royal secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
And Ira from Jair was David's priest and chief official.
